findings.title: The model-name cleanup misses the `[1m]` suffix shown in the linked issue.
findings.body: The issue's example `llm_request` span has `model: "claude-opus-4-6[1m]"`, with a closing `]`. This looks like Claude Code's marker for the 1M-context variant, not an ANSI escape. Neither regex matches it: `ANSI_SGR_RE` needs a leading ESC character, and `/\[[0-9;]*m$/` needs the string to end in `m`. So `gen_ai.request.model` becomes `claude-opus-4-6[1m]`, and model and pricing lookups will likely fail for those spans. The test only covers `\u001b[1m`, which does not appear in the issue data. Fix: also strip a trailing `\[[0-9;]*m\]` (or `[1m]`), and add a test that uses the exact string from the issue.

findings.title: Any span with a `span.type` attribute now passes the LLM export filter.
findings.body: `span.type` is a common key outside Claude Code. For example, Datadog-style instrumentation sets it to `web`, `http`, `db` or `cache`. Because the check looks only at the key name, all of those non-LLM spans now count as GenAI spans and get exported by default. That undoes the smart filter's job of dropping generic HTTP and DB spans. Fix: match on the value as well, e.g. accept `span.type` only when it is `interaction` or `llm_request`. This is the same check the ingest side uses in `expandClaudeCodeSpanAttributes`.
